clue.text: Foreign bird may be found nesting in such UK areas

indicators.note: something nesting in a place sits snugly inside it, so look for the answer lying within the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the three words, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports that an exotic species may nest in certain British regions.
explanation.definitionFit: The chukar is a partridge native to Asia and the Middle East, so to a British reader it is a bird from abroad.

clue.text: Worthless residue placed in river, tumour operated on (12, two words)

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A grim surgical note: something dumped in a river after a tumour was removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed' looks like a link to the river, but it supplies its own letters to go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Caput mortuum, Latin for 'dead head', was the alchemists' term for the useless dregs left after distillation.

clue.text: Dance music, suitable for singing with 150 around

indicators.note: the answer is what remains when the Roman number placed around it is stripped away from the longer word

parts.note: music written for a choir is choral

explanation.walkthrough: This clue works backwards: the answer is what sits inside the longer word once the Roman number around it is accounted for.

clue.text: By common consent gun topped and tailed wading bird (7, two words)

explanation.surface: Everyone agreed that the gun shot both ends off a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped and tailed' looks like one instruction for one word, but it is split between the weapon and the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Una voce is Latin for 'with one voice', meaning unanimously, by general agreement.

clue.text: King repeatedly favoured preservative for flowers

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
favoured means in, as in 'in favour', and repeatedly doubles it

explanation.surface: A monarch kept choosing the same thing to keep his cut flowers fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinins are plant hormones that delay ageing in cut flowers and leaves, so they act as a preservative.

clue.text: Red Sea turned a pale green

indicators.note: turned suggests the words are churned about, so their letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Reseda, named after the mignonette plant, is a greyish pale green shade.

clue.text: Subdue regressive interdicts restricting clubs

to restrict is to hem in, so the card suit is held inside

parts.note: tabus, a variant spelling of taboos, are prohibitions

explanation.surface: Reactionary bans that limit clubs are used to subdue people.
explanation.definitionFit: Subact is an archaic verb meaning to bring under, reduce or subdue, from Latin subigere.

clue.text: Stand-up routine, moment after silence?

indicators.note: after sets the order of the pieces, so the word for a moment goes second, behind the call for quiet

a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A comedian's act: the pause before the punchline lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtick, from Yiddish, is a performer's signature comic routine or gimmick.

clue.text: Feels very hot going round uni in hooded cape

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so the outer word wraps the university

parts.note: someone who feels very hot burns
OU is the Open University, a British distance-learning university

explanation.surface: Someone sweltering as they walk around campus wearing a hooded cloak.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnous is the long hooded cloak worn by Arabs and Berbers in North Africa.

clue.text: Cheers marking appearance of princess in bustle?

Di is Princess Diana

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bustle' looks like the Victorian dress padding; it is commotion. 'Cheers' here is the British farewell, not applause.
explanation.definitionFit: Addio is Italian for goodbye, and cheers is informal British for goodbye.

clue.text: Like uppish pro in company, his voice can't be natural

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pro' is short for prostitute here, not professional.

clue.text: Former Scots parliamentary constituents: reset these at falling out (12, two words)

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: The old Scottish Parliament was made up of three estates: clergy, nobility and burgh commissioners, sitting together.

clue.text: Nothing requiring fine discrimination should be postponed (5, two words)

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

clue.text: Seat on Jumbo most of time caused to go back

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumbo' suggests an aeroplane, but it is an elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A houdah, or howdah, is the canopied seat carried on an elephant's back.

clue.text: Father wants ordinary people to replace a practical joker

indicators.note: one thing replacing another takes its slot, so the new word goes where the single letter was

the ranks are ordinary soldiers or people, as opposed to officers
taken as written; this is the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A dad wishes ordinary folk would stand in for a practical joker.
explanation.definitionFit: A prankster is someone who plays tricks or practical jokes on people.

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

clue.text: Minimal beachwear creating some mirth on Guernsey

explanation.surface: Skimpy swimwear causing amusement on a Channel Island beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a very small swimsuit or bikini bottom with a strip at the back.

clue.text: Dance: ungainly lump almost finished one twice

a means one

clue.text: Sculptor in the manner that incorporates regular feature of his work!

clue.text: Work for the gutter press and create fight for Spooner?

running amok is being in a frenzy

explanation.definitionFit: A komatik is an Inuit sledge, traditionally built with wooden runners.

clue.text: Creeper favoured as feed for African animal

clue.text: Reverses large tub, then starts off

sets off, or begins

explanation.definitionFit: A backset is a setback or reverse, a check to progress.

clue.text: Airport fails? Lacking terminal thus I first get lost there

get lost means vanish, so these letters are taken away from the pool

parts.note: taken as written, the full letter pool
taken as written, the letters that disappear

clue.text: Bits of armour no good for leg in the way of sword thrusts?

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Senior cleric accepted books, part of holy scripture
